messages.subject: Problem with RmaCnPlm
parts:
Dear Henrik,

I am trying to summarize two 250K_Nsp chips with RmaCnPlm but I get
the following error:

> fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
<simpleError in .Call("R_rlm_rma_default_model", y, psiCode, psiK,
PACKAGE = "affyPLM"): C symbol name "R_rlm_rma_default_model" not in
DLL for package "affyPLM">
Error en list("fit(plm, verbose = verbose)" = <environment>,
"fit.ProbeLevelModel(plm, verbose = verbose)" = <environment>, :

where the object plm is

RmaCnPlm:
Data set: casosLola
Chip type: Mapping250K_Nsp
Input tags: QN
Output tags: QN,RMA,A+B
Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm"; shift: num 0; flavor: chr
"affyPLM"; treatNAsAs: chr "weights"; mergeStrands: logi TRUE;
combineAlleles: logi TRUE).
Path: plmData/casosLola,QN,RMA,A+B/Mapping250K_Nsp
RAM: 0.00MB

Please, can you tell me whether is a bug or a error in my setup.
Find my sessionInfo bellow.
Best regards. Olivier

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Problem with RmaCnPlm
parts:
Hi Olivier,

thanks for the note. I tracked it down and it only happens if you run
affyPLM >= v1.13.9 (which you get if you run R v2.6.0 and installed
recently). The reason is that Ben Bolstad migrated more of his code
in affyPLM into preprocessCore - I know he planned to do this at some
stage. I've been running affyPLM v1.13.6, so I didn't notice the
update. I'll try to provide an update later today (my time).

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with RmaCnPlm
parts:
Hi,

hmm... that does not make sense to me, because that piece of code
reported should not be in the package anymore. First, close all R
sessions and try to reinstall. You don't have to delete any
directories. I assume you are still using the RmaCnPlm class,
correct?

Then if you get the same error again here are some troubleshooting questions:

1) Did you restart R between the installs?

2) Did you save a workspace image?

3) What does packageDescription("aroma.affymetrix")[1:3] return?

4) What does this return?

code <- capture.output(getFitFunction.RmaPlm)
rows <- grep(".Call", code)
print(code[sort(c(rows,rows+1))])

5) I would also recomment you turn on verbose output, e.g.
verbose=-10, and report what you get because that will help us too.
Email message are free, so cut'n'paste more than just the last line.

Cheers

/Henrik

PS. For ExonRmaPlm users: I forgot to update that code, so there the
bug remains. I'll provide a patch soon. DS.
